items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: But when I was like 12 or 13 I heard a Horace Silver record. And it really just stunned me.

ctx.x: You said in around 1990 during one of your presentations, you have a desire to demystify the world of jazz. Jazz musicians are just like the rest of us only more so. Can you expand on that a tad?

Sure. I first fell in love with the music when I was like, well that’s not fair ‘cause when I was really little I liked boogie-woogie and that’s pretty close to jazz. And just the drive and forward momentum of it felt so good when you’re an 8-year-old kid man, I loved that. But when I was like 12 or 13 I heard a Horace Silver record. And it really just stunned me. I thought who are these people? Where are they? How can I find out what they’re doing? What is this thing they’re doing? Because you’ve got to remember…

difficult really, that I would say everybody that I ran into coming up was very accommodating. They weren’t overly friendly necessarily, but they respected the effort that you had to put in to try to be a player. And I found also their sense of humor is what got them through the life and the music, it’s kind of a foxhole sense of humor.
